title: An Invocation's location in the Atlas document tree is its status, not a field it carries
content:
Every primitive's `In Progress Invocations` section states the movement rule explicitly. A.6.1.1.1.2.6.1.5: "Once an Invocation is successfully completed, its subtree will be moved to A.6.1.1.1.2.6.1.3 - Active Instances." A.6.1.1.1.2.6.2.1.4 adds the failure branch: "Invocations that are completed successfully are moved to the Active Instances Directory, whereas failed Invocations are Archived in the Hub Data Repository."

The archive is itself partitioned by *reason* for exit — `Failed Invocations` and `Suspended Instances` are separate destinations (A.6.1.1.1.2.6.2.1.5.1.1 and .5.1.2), so an instance that never launched is filed apart from one that launched and was stopped.

Moving the subtree rather than flipping a status flag makes the two representations impossible to desynchronize. There is no way for a document to claim `Active` while sitting under `In Progress`, because the claim *is* the placement. It also means the tree is always a valid census: counting live exposures is a matter of enumerating one subtree's children.

The trade-off is that history becomes path-dependent. A stable identifier survives the move, but any reference by location breaks, and reconstructing an instance's lifecycle requires knowing which sections it passed through rather than reading a log in place.
description: Completed Invocations have their subtree physically moved to Active Instances and failed ones to the Hub Data Repository, so status cannot drift out of sync with placement.
